My neighbor Loretta Puckett turned 74 last March and she keeps a stack of books on a TV tray beside her front door for anyone who wants one.

That's just who she is.

Every time I walk past her house on Dellwood Circle in Macon, Georgia, that little tray has something new on it. Sometimes it's a paperback thriller with the spine cracked. Sometimes it's a Reader's Digest from 1997. Sometimes it's a cookbook with a sticky note on the front that says "Good recipes inside, Loretta" in her looping handwriting, like she's signing a letter.

I found a photograph of my husband in a junk drawer last March and I sat down on the kitchen floor and cried for 40 minutes.

Not because he was dead. He was upstairs. I could hear the recliner squeaking through the ceiling.

I cried because the man in the photograph wasn't the man upstairs anymore. And I hadn't realized when I'd lost him.
